items.title: @waline/client vulnerable to stored XSS through unsanitized comment edit previews
items.summary: ### Summary `@waline/client` renders the comment editor's live preview with `marked` and no sanitizer (`utils/markdown.ts`), and the preview is injected with `v-html`. When a comment is edited, the editor is seeded with the comment's raw, un-sanitized body (`orig`). Only administrators and the comment owner can edit. So an administrator who clicks Edit on an attacker's comment renders that attacker's raw HTML in their own session: an unauthenticated commenter achieves privilege-escalation stored

items.title: soapbar: verify_envelope_bsp accepts an unauthenticated embedded certificate (signature forgery / authentication bypass)
items.summary: ### Impact `verify_envelope_bsp()` derived its trust anchor from the message it was verifying. It read the X.509 certificate out of the caller-untrusted `wsse:BinarySecurityToken`, validated **only** that certificate's not-before / not-after dates, and then verified the signature against that same certificate. items.title: TwigView FileLoader may allow arbitrary file reads through user-controlled template paths
items.summary: ### Impact If `FileLoader::findTemplate()` is supplied un-validated user controlled data, arbitrary files can be read. ### Patches 1.3.3 and 2.1.2 contain a fix for this issue. ### Workarounds Don't supply user controlled data to `include` and `extends` tags.

items.title: GitHub CLI gh codespace jupyter may allow code execution via unvalidated URLs from malicious Codespaces
items.summary: ### Summary A security vulnerability has been identified in GitHub CLI that could allow remote code execution when users connect to a malicious Codespace using the `gh codespace jupyter` command. The command opens JupyterLab by launching a URL in the user's browser, but that URL is supplied by a process running inside the Codespace and the CLI opens it without validating it. items.title: github.com/insomniacslk/dhcp permits denial of service through a malformed IPv4 payload length
items.summary: In github.com/insomniacslk/dhcp/dhcpv4/nclient4, BroadcastRawUDPConn.ReadFrom does not validate that the IPv4 payload length is sufficient to hold a UDP header before calculating the DHCP payload length. A frame with an IPv4 total-length field specifying fewer than eight payload bytes results in a negative DHCP length, causing a panic in buf.Consume due to a negative slice bound.

items.title: etcd: CRL enforcement bypass on gRPC listener when `--listen-client-http-urls` is configured
items.summary: ### Impact _What kind of vulnerability is it? Who is impacted?_ When etcd is configured with `--listen-client-http-urls` to split the HTTP and gRPC client endpoints onto separate listeners, the `--client-crl-file` Certificate Revocation List is not enforced on the gRPC listener. A client presenting a revoked certificate is correctly rejected by the HTTP endpoint but continues to authenticate successfully over gRPC. ### Patches _Has the problem been patched? items.title: Cakephp twig-view unserialize Twig filter allows arbitrary object deserialization
items.summary: ### Impact The `unserialize` filter has no restriction on which classes are allowed. This can be used as a deserialization remote-code-execution gadget. ### Patches 1.3.3 and 2.1.2 contain a fix for this issue. The fix may impact backwards compatibility if you are relying on deserializing PHP objects in your templates. ### Workarounds Don't use the `unserialize` filter.
